subproblems.title: Continuous functions are bounded and integrable on the open unit cube
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, let Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) carry Lebesgue measure (volume), and let Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}. If f : Euclid k → ℝ is continuous, then (a) there is M ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| ≤ M for every y ∈ Q₁, and (b) f is integrable on Q₁.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), Continuous f → (∃ M : ℝ, ∀ y ∈ {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |f y| ≤ M) ∧ IntegrableOn f {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof (bv_trace: 'div G is continuous; it is therefore bounded on the compact set [0, 1]ⁿ ⊇ Q₁') and step 1 ('Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ; so v_k ... integrable'). Both uses are isolated here for an arbitrary continuous f.

Notation. Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Lebesgue measure volume; y_i is the i-th coordinate (y i = WithLp.ofLp y i in Lean). Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} and K := {y : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i} (the closed unit cube).

1. K is compact. The coordinate map ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ), y ↦ (y_i)_i, is a homeomorphism (Mathlib PiLp.homeomorph 2 (fun _ => ℝ)). A point y lies in K iff 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for every i, i.e. iff ofLp y lies in the order interval Icc 0 1 = ∏_i [0, 1] of Fin k → ℝ (the order there is coordinatewise). So K is the preimage of Icc 0 1 under this homeomorphism. Icc 0 1 is compact in Fin k → ℝ (isCompact_Icc; it is a finite product of compact intervals), and the preimage of a compact set under a homeomorphism is compact (Homeomorph.isCompact_preimage). Hence K is compact.

2. Q₁ ⊆ K, since 0 < y_i < 1 implies 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for each i.

3. Boundedness. f is continuous, hence continuous on the compact set K, so it is bounded there: there is M ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| = ‖f(y)‖ ≤ M for all y ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). By step 2 the same bound holds for all y ∈ Q₁. This proves (a).

4. Integrability. Lebesgue measure on Euclid k is finite on compact sets (it is an additive Haar measure, so IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts holds), and Euclid k is Hausdorff. Hence f, continuous on the compact set K, is integrable on K (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact). Integrability on a set passes to subsets (IntegrableOn.mono_set), so by step 2 f is integrable on Q₁. This proves (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: The closed cube K = {0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1} is the preimage of the compact box Icc 0 1 ⊆ (Fin k → ℝ) under the homeomorphism PiLp.homeomorph, hence compact.
A continuous f is bounded on the compact K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn), hence on Q₁.
A continuous f is integrable on the compact K for the Haar measure volume (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact), hence on Q₁ ⊆ K.

subproblems.title: An affine bound in ∫|v_k| passes to the L¹ limit against a bounded multiplier
subproblems.statement: Let (α, μ) be a measure space (α : Type with a σ-algebra), S ⊆ α a measurable set, v_k : α → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ), w, h : α → ℝ, and A, B, M ∈ ℝ with B ≥ 0. Assume: every v_k and w are integrable on S; h is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ restricted to S; |h(x)| ≤ M for every x ∈ S; ∫_S |v_k − w| dμ → 0 as k → ∞; and |∫_S v_k h dμ| ≤ A + B ∫_S |v_k| dμ for every k. Then |∫_S w h dμ| ≤ A + B ∫_S |w| dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (S : Set α) (v : ℕ → α → ℝ) (w h : α → ℝ) (A B M : ℝ), MeasurableSet S → 0 ≤ B → (∀ k, IntegrableOn (v k) S μ) → IntegrableOn w S μ → AEStronglyMeasurable h (μ.restrict S) → (∀ x ∈ S, |h x| ≤ M) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ k, |∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ| ≤ A + B * ∫ x in S, |v k x| ∂μ) → |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ| ≤ A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (bv_trace: 'Limit k → ∞ ... Passing to the limit in the inequality of step 1'), stated for an arbitrary measure space, set S, multiplier h and constants A, B. In the parent it is applied with S = Q_δ, h = div G, A = (2n + 1)V and B = 4n.

Notation. All integrals are over S with respect to μ, i.e. Bochner integrals for the restricted measure μ⌞S. Put ε_k := ∫_S |v_k − w|.

1. A.e. bound and integrability of the products. S is measurable and |h(x)| ≤ M for every x ∈ S, so ‖h(x)‖ = |h(x)| ≤ M for μ⌞S-almost every x (ae_restrict_iff'). Since h is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞S and essentially bounded by M there, and w and every v_k are integrable on S, the products w·h and v_k·h are integrable on S (Integrable.mul_bdd: integrable times essentially bounded a.e.-strongly measurable is integrable).

2. Difference estimate. Fix k. By linearity (step 1), ∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h = ∫_S (w h − v_k h). Hence
|∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ ∫_S |w h − v_k h|.
For μ⌞S-a.e. x, |w(x)h(x) − v_k(x)h(x)| = |w(x) − v_k(x)|·|h(x)| ≤ M·|v_k(x) − w(x)|, using |h(x)| ≤ M (step 1), |w − v_k| = |v_k − w| and |v_k − w| ≥ 0. Both |w h − v_k h| and M|v_k − w| are integrable on S (step 1 and integrability of v_k − w), so monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono_ae) and linearity give
|∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ ∫_S M|v_k − w| = M ε_k.

3. Comparison of ∫|v_k| with ∫|w|. For every x, |v_k(x)| = |w(x) + (v_k(x) − w(x))| ≤ |w(x)| + |v_k(x) − w(x)|. The functions |v_k|, |w| and |v_k − w| are integrable on S, so ∫_S |v_k| ≤ ∫_S (|w| + |v_k − w|) = ∫_S |w| + ε_k.

4. Estimate for fixed k. By the triangle inequality, the hypothesis on v_k, step 3 multiplied by B ≥ 0, and step 2:
|∫_S w h| ≤ |∫_S v_k h| + |∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h|
 ≤ A + B∫_S |v_k| + M ε_k
 ≤ A + B∫_S |w| + B ε_k + M ε_k
 = A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M) ε_k.

5. Limit. Since ε_k → 0, the sequence A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M) ε_k converges to A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M)·0 = A + B∫_S |w|. By step 4 the constant |∫_S w h| is ≤ every term of this sequence, so it is ≤ its limit (ge_of_tendsto'): |∫_S w h| ≤ A + B∫_S |w|. ∎
proof_key_steps: |h| ≤ M on the measurable set S gives an a.e. bound for μ⌞S, so w·h and v_k·h are integrable on S.
|∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ ∫_S |w − v_k||h| ≤ M ε_k with ε_k = ∫_S |v_k − w|.
Hence |∫_S w h| ≤ A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M) ε_k for every k (B ≥ 0).

subproblems.title: Set integrals over the shrunken cubes Q_δ converge to the integral over Q₁ as δ ↓ 0
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Lebesgue measure, Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} and, for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {z : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}. If f : Euclid k → ℝ is integrable on Q₁, then ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺ (i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), IntegrableOn f {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → Tendsto (fun δ : ℝ => ∫ y in {z : Euclid k | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, f y) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, f y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (bv_trace: 'Limit δ ↓ 0. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 4) ∈ (0, 1/4], δ_j ↓ 0; every point of Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. ... By dominated convergence, ∫_{Q_{δ_j}} w div G → ∫_{Q₁} w div G'), stated for an arbitrary f integrable on Q₁ (dominated by |f| instead of M|w|) and along the filter δ → 0⁺, which contains the parent's sequence δ_j = 1/(j + 4) → 0⁺ as a special case.

Notation. Euclid k with Lebesgue measure volume; y_i is the i-th coordinate; Q₁ and Q_δ as in the statement (so Q₁ is the case a = 0, b = 1 and Q_δ the case a = δ, b = 1 − δ of the sets {z : a < z_i < b for all i}). 1_E denotes the indicator function of E.

1. Openness and measurability. For a, b ∈ ℝ, {z : a < z_i < b for all i} = ⋂_{i ∈ Fin k} ({z : a < z_i} ∩ {z : z_i < b}). Each coordinate map z ↦ z_i is continuous (PiLp.continuous_apply), so each {z : a < z_i} and {z : z_i < b} is open, and a finite intersection of open sets is open (isOpen_iInter_of_finite). Hence Q₁ and every Q_δ are open, in particular Borel measurable.

2. Inclusion. If δ ≥ 0 then Q_δ ⊆ Q₁: from δ < z_i < 1 − δ we get 0 ≤ δ < z_i and z_i < 1 − δ ≤ 1.

3. Reduction to a fixed measure. Let δ > 0; the set (0, ∞) of such δ belongs to 𝓝[>] 0. Since Q_δ is measurable and Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (steps 1–2), ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q₁ ∩ Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q_δ} f (setIntegral_indicator and Q₁ ∩ Q_δ = Q_δ). So the functions δ ↦ ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f and δ ↦ ∫_{Q_δ} f agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and it suffices (Tendsto.congr') to prove ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺.

4. Dominated convergence. Apply the dominated convergence theorem for the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) to the measure volume⌞Q₁, the functions F_δ := 1_{Q_δ} f, the limit f and the bound |f|:
 (a) every F_δ is a.e.-strongly measurable for volume⌞Q₁, because f is (it is integrable on Q₁) and Q_δ is measurable (step 1);
 (b) |F_δ(y)| ≤ |f(y)| for every y and δ (norm of an indicator);
 (c) |f| is integrable on Q₁ because f is;
 (d) for volume⌞Q₁-a.e. y — namely for every y ∈ Q₁, which suffices because Q₁ is measurable (ae_restrict_iff') — F_δ(y) → f(y) as δ → 0⁺. Indeed, fix y ∈ Q₁ and i ∈ Fin k. Since 0 < y_i and 0 < 1 − y_i, every δ in a neighbourhood of 0 satisfies δ < y_i and δ < 1 − y_i, i.e. δ < y_i < 1 − δ; restricting to 𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0 this holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. Fin k is finite, so these finitely many eventualities hold simultaneously (Filter.eventually_all): eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, y ∈ Q_δ, and then F_δ(y) = f(y). So δ ↦ F_δ(y) is eventually equal to the constant f(y), hence converges to f(y).
 Dominated convergence gives ∫_{Q₁} F_δ → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺, and by step 3, ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each set {z : a < z_i < b ∀ i} is a finite intersection of open coordinate half-spaces, so Q₁ and all Q_δ are open and measurable.
For δ ≥ 0, Q_δ ⊆ Q₁, so for δ > 0, ∫_{Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f.
Every y ∈ Q₁ lies in Q_δ for all sufficiently small δ > 0 (finitely many coordinates; Filter.eventually_all), so 1_{Q_δ} f → f pointwise on Q₁.
Dominated convergence along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0 with bound |f| (integrable on Q₁) gives ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f.
